st.headline: Hours after retrenchment: How to stretch your dollar and avoid cash flow issues
st.teaser: The NTUC PME and MoneyOwl playbook aims to help workers strengthen their finances and plan ahead.
fullText: SINGAPORE – When Sunena Sharma was retrenched a few years ago, all she could think about was whether she had enough cash and savings to tide her family through several months.
“My role in a technology company was made redundant following a restructuring exercise. It was an emotional roller-coaster,” said the 47-year-old.
Her experience reflects a wider conversation about what employees can do to strengthen their finances while still being employed and how best to navigate the stresses of losing one’s income.

For workers who have gone through retrenchment, receiving timely support within the first few hours of losing their jobs is key. This includes immediately checking how long one’s savings can last and exploring ways to earn a temporary income.

Workers can now pick up a financial tip or two from the second edition of Navigating Retrenchment, a guide by NTUC PME and financial advisory firm MoneyOwl that focuses on equipping employees with the financial preparedness they need.
NTUC PME aims to provide targeted support for professionals, managers and executives.
Director of NTUC PME Wendy Tan said they saw the need to come together to develop a playbook that helps workers build their financial resilience.
“When someone is retrenched, they don’t just worry about their next job, they may also struggle with the psychological consequences as well as face financial pressures,” she said.

Employees can proactively build an emergency fund while still being employed to strengthen their finances and ease the transition, said the writers in the playbook. “Every dollar you set aside gives you room to breathe. Even if retrenchment never comes, you build lasting, better habits.”

The guide recommends setting aside six to nine months of essential expenses in cash or liquid savings, and trimming discretionary spending such as dining out, entertainment and travel as early as possible.

It is also recommended to preserve cash and prioritise cash flow over cost savings, where necessary. This means spreading out expenses such as paying for home mortgages from their Central Provident Fund Ordinary Accounts instead of cash, and converting annual subscriptions and renewals to monthly payments.

Employees should also avoid risky investments and review their insurance policies to check for overpayment and under-coverage. They should consider adding low-cost term life or critical illness insurance first to maintain coverage, even if it means dropping some expensive policies.

When retrenchment is announced, it is important to secure a formal termination letter before checking every component of the compensation settlement, such as retrenchment benefits, notice pay, and annual leave and bonuses.
“Do not sign any agreement before reviewing it carefully,” said the experts in the playbook.

Retrenched employees who are National Trades Union Congress members can contact the labour movement or their respective unions to negotiate and secure a retrenchment package. Non-members can approach the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management for mediation.
When Sunena was retrenched, she failed to negotiate for retrenchment benefits with the company, and approached NTUC for support.

“I was advised on how to position my contributions, circumstances and expectations professionally and firmly. I was able to negotiate an improved separation package that included additional ex-gratia payment and a prorated bonus,” she said.
After receiving the payout, employees should preserve it and keep it liquid in savings, fixed deposits or Singapore Savings Bonds, said the writers in the playbook.
Can you ensure that your emergency fund can last until you find a new job? Including the payout, how many months of expenses does it cover?

The playbook recommends comparing liquid assets against monthly expenses first, and starting by listing them out, including cash, fixed deposits, T-bills and Singapore Savings Bonds. The aim is to have between six and nine months of savings.

Employees can reduce their monthly expenses by lowering grocery bills, reducing utility costs and cooking at home more frequently instead of dining out. They can also consider whether larger household expenses such as a car or domestic helper remain essential.
Another tip is to pause recurring savings investment plans to free up cash flow, which is usually penalty-free.

There are generally a few traps to avoid, such as committing to new savings plans, trying to make quick cash through gambling, crypto or risky stocks, or falling for job offer scams that ask for upfront payment.
“Trying to make a quick buck out of panic almost always backfires and can wipe out savings in days,” noted the writers in the playbook.
Employees can tap available retrenchment resources including government schemes and community support to bridge the gap while actively finding a new job.

The SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme allows eligible employees who have lost their jobs involuntarily to secure temporary payouts of up to $6,000 over six months. As part of another scheme, Singaporeans aged 40 and above can receive up to $3,000 in monthly training allowance for selected full-time courses, up to a cap of $72,000 per worker.
There are community groups such as ComCare that provide grants to lower-income retrenched households .

For assistance with housing loans, it is worth noting that the Homeowner Job Support pilot can defer or reduce instalments and suspend interest for up to 12 months if the home owners are unemployed and working with a career coach.
Retrenched workers can also ask their banks about refinancing to lower their monthly commitment.
Another recommendation is to explore earning a temporary income, such as renting out a room, or considering side hustles or part-time work that keep professional skills sharp.

cna.headline: Hong Kong exchange to launch Shein derivatives after trading debut next week
cna.teaser: Hong Kong exchange to launch Shein derivatives after trading debut next week
fullText: Aug 28 : Hong Kong's bourse operator will allow short selling of Shein's shares after the fast-fashion retailer makes its trading debut on September 1 as well as launch weekly and monthly options and derivative warrants, it said on Friday.

• Shein weekly and monthly options will begin trading on September 1, with monthly contracts expiring in September, October, November and December this year, as well as March, June and September next year.
• The options contracts will have a contract size of 500 shares. Weekly contracts will expire on September 4 and September 11.
• The simultaneous launch of options, warrants and short-selling on Shein's listing day gives investors immediate trading and hedging tools, potentially boosting liquidity and price discovery.

• Shein is set to price its initial public offering near the midpoint of its marketed range at HK$48.56 a share, valuing the company at roughly $26.5 billion, Reuters reported on Thursday, citing two people with knowledge of the matter.
Our chief editor shares analysis and picks of the week's biggest news every Saturday.

economistArticle.title: The Price of Closed Borders: The Impending Cost of America's Labor Crackdown
paras: Any large-scale tightening of immigration policies invariably leaves an indelible mark on an economy’s structural foundations. In the United States, proposed measures to curtail the influx of both high-skilled and low-skilled workers threaten to dismantle the delicate equilibrium of its labor market. For decades, foreign-born workers have acted as a crucial demographic buffer, filling vacancies in sectors ranging from agricultural picking to software development, which native-born workers frequently bypass.

The immediate consequence of a sudden contraction in the labor force is a sharp contraction in potential output. When firms cannot source the necessary talent, they are forced to scale back production plans or defer capital investments. This bottleneck is not merely frictional; it represents a permanent downshifting of America’s economic growth trajectory. Agricultural fields in California may lie fallow, and tech startups in Silicon Valley may relocate their research hubs to more hospitable jurisdictions like Vancouver or London.

Moreover, the economic fallout is amplified by the inflationary pressures that labor scarcity generates. As businesses scramble to outbid each other for a dwindling pool of eligible workers, wages are bid up without a corresponding increase in productivity. These escalating labor costs inevitably feed into consumer prices, complicating the Federal Reserve's delicate task of maintaining price stability. Rather than fostering a high-wage, high-productivity utopia, a labor supply shock threatens to induce a stagflationary squeeze on households.

Proponents of immigration curbs argue that such restrictions will spur domestic automation and compel companies to invest more heavily in their existing workforce. However, this optimistic view overlooks the sheer speed at which these policies are enacted. Automation is a capital-intensive, multi-year endeavor that cannot be easily retrofitted overnight. In the interim, small and medium-sized enterprises, which operate on wafer-thin margins, are likely to bear the brunt of the shock, leading to business closures rather than technological upgrades.

Ultimately, a country’s economic power is a function of its demographics and its innovation. By restricting the inflow of global talent and labor, the world’s largest economy risks self-sabotage. The true cost of a tighter border is not merely measured in the enforcement budget, but in the lost growth, diminished dynamism, and reduced global competitiveness that will haunt America for decades to come.
economistArticle.cn:
任何大规模收紧移民政策的行为，都不可避免地会对一个经济体的结构基础留下难以磨灭的烙印。在美国，拟议中的限制高技能和低技能劳工流入的措施，正威胁到其劳动力市场脆弱的均衡状态。几十年来，外籍劳工一直发挥着关键的人口缓冲作用，填补了从农业采摘到软件开发等本国劳工往往避开的行业空缺。

劳动力突然萎缩的直接后果是潜在产出的急剧收缩。当企业无法寻得所需人才时，它们不得不缩减生产计划或推迟资本投资。这种瓶颈不仅是摩擦性的，它代表着美国经济增长轨迹的永久性下移。加利福尼亚的农田可能会荒芜，硅谷的科技初创企业可能会将其研发中心搬迁到温哥华或伦敦等更具包容性的司法管辖区。

此外，劳动力短缺所引发的通胀压力，会放大其经济负面效应。随着企业争先恐后地竞价争取人数不断减少的合规员工，工资水平被推高，但生产率却没有相应提高。这些不断上升的劳动力成本必然传导至消费价格，从而使美联储维持价格稳定的微妙任务变得更加复杂。劳动力供给冲击非但无法培育出高工资、高生产率的理想国，反而有可能对家庭造成滞胀性挤压。

移民限制的支持者认为，此类限制将刺激国内自动化，并迫使公司加大对其现有员工队伍的投入。然而，这种乐观的观点忽略了这些政策颁布的速度。自动化是一项资本密集型、耗时多年的工程，不可能在夜之间轻易完成改造。在此过渡期间，在微薄利润边缘运营的中小型企业可能会承受这一冲击的绝大部分影响，从而导致企业倒闭而非技术升级。

归根结底，一个国家的经济实力是其人口结构和创新能力的体现。通过限制全球人才和劳动力的流入，这个世界最大的经济体面临着自我伤害的风险。边境收紧的真实代价不仅体现在执法预算上，还体现在失去的增长、减弱的活力和降低的全球竞争力上，这些将在未来数十年里困扰美国。

This sentence uses a dynamic subordinate clause starting with 'As' to establish cause and effect, vividly conveying a sense of market urgency. It demonstrates how macroeconomic forces directly impact real-world business decisions.
